briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Underwater, Momentum Overhead: Michigan Weed Eyes Relief as Feds Edge Toward Rescheduling
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax is collecting a fraction of what Lansing projected, adding fuel to a gubernatorial candidate's repeal pledge, while home-state chain JARS keeps expanding out west. Nationally, the FDA is racing to approve psychedelic therapies and a federal court just upheld medical marijuana's Schedule III status, even as the broader DEA rescheduling decision remains in limbo.

local.text: JARS Cannabis expands into largest Arizona chain — JARS Cannabis, the Michigan-based chain, announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa brand dispensaries, which will soon make JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

Menominee petition could add four dispensaries — A pending petition drive could lead to four more dispensaries in the city of Menominee, raising the local cap from nine to 13 stores, with organizers saying they turned in more than enough signatures for the November ballot.
Metro Times crowns Michigan's best flower and shops — The Detroit Metro Times staff picked their favorite Michigan flower, rosin, vapes, prerolls, edibles, and dispensaries of the year.

Wholesale tax revenue running far below forecast — Michigan's 24% wholesale marijuana tax is still only bringing in a fraction of what state officials projected, generating about $37 million in the second quarter of 2026 and roughly $34 million in the first, against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter.

GOP nominee vows to repeal 24% tax — John James, the Republican candidate in Michigan's governor's race, said he supports repealing the state's 24% wholesale cannabis tax, telling donors he wants to "repeal or sharply reduce" the levy.

national.text: FDA fast-tracks psilocybin and PTSD drug reviews — The FDA issued national priority vouchers to three companies studying psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression and major depressive disorder, plus methylone, a drug similar to MDMA, for PTSD.

Court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III move — Reclassification opponents' lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's change in schedule was rebuffed this month in federal court, as the D.C. Circuit left the rescheduling order in effect, holding that opponents hadn't shown likely success.

Trulieve makes history with NYSE listing — Trulieve Cannabis Corp. received approval to list on the New York Stock Exchange, paving its path to the major exchange by restructuring to maintain a 100-percent medical footprint following federal Schedule III reclassification.
Curaleaf bids $4 a share for Aurora — August 2026 cannabis M&A moved into a different weight class, with Curaleaf announcing a US$4 per share takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis on August 10.

DEA hearing wraps, decision on rescheduling still pending — In its own final brief the DEA argued marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, though practitioners tracking the docket place a final answer somewhere in late 2026 or 2027.
